chapter_title: Concerning the Summons, in which Limb of the Soul it descended to the First Man.
chapter_note: The chapter is overwhelmingly cosmological-correspondential teaching about the First Man as Head and the scattered Living Soul as limbs, with systematic body↔cosmos analogy and a fivefold faculty list. It is embedded in a late Q&A dialogue frame (teachers/enlightener) and contains one citation-like appeal to “scriptures” in the question, but no clear NT/Gospel entry vector. The second-half “drift” here reads more as narrative elaboration than institutional/pastoral graft.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Hagiographic/compilation frame: “Once again… questioned the enlightener… He says…” + a question. The clause “it is written in the scriptures” is a citation posture, but not clearly NT-derived here; the whole paragraph functions as dialogue apparatus, not substrate exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: “Indeed, the First Man dispersed himself and he [...] limb of the living soul [...] of the living soul; he has [...] he did not know [... ...] but the blessed, glorious Man came [in] secret; in his image; in his shape; in his love; in his holy virgin, she who is the virgin of light, the soul of the father.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution: “The [enli]ghtener speaks:”. Removed self-referential scribal/authorial aside: “as I have written for you [...]” as a likely compilation-era pointer to a written corpus rather than the impersonal substrate voice.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core cosmology (First Man dispersal; Virgin of Light; ‘soul of the father’) is embedded inside a late dialogue attribution. The ‘I have written for you’ gesture breaks the impersonal, system-internal explanatory voice and looks like compilation-era cross-reference.

paragraphs.core_text: “After the fashion of this fleshly body: as the root of all the limbs hang upon the head, so that should one of the person's limbs be cut off, while the head exists he has hope for [...] but if his head should be cut off, the entire body will die and he is lost.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal correspondential instruction: body anatomy (head/limbs) as the fixed image for a cosmic dependency relation. No citation, exhortation, or institutional targeting; mapping stays cosmos↔body-image.

paragraphs.core_text: “This is also the case for the Firs[t] Ma[n]. He is the head, while his sons attach to it the limbs [of] his soul. Or, conversely, like the living air, on which all flesh entirely lives as it breathes and [...] therein. His head is placed on the body of the Pillar of Glory in the heights of the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: System-internal mapping: First Man=head; sons/limbs=soul; living air analogy; Pillar of Glory located ‘in the heights of the universe’. This is classic cosmological correspondential exposition, not application.

paragraphs.core_text: “[This i]s also the case [for] the father, the blessed Man; as he is like the head that is upon the body and the air that upon the Pillar is set i[n ...] being made strong by his light virgin, [she] who is his soul that he clothes [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the same correspondence chain (head/body/air/Pillar) with the Light-Virgin/soul motif. Despite lacunae, the register remains cosmic and structural.

paragraphs.core_text: “[ ... ] t[h]ose [...]: the mind, thought, insight, counsel and c[on]sideration that he produced and sent forth from hi[m to] do his will. He sprang and travelled behind them. [...] of his living soul, which is entwined among the rebels; as they are like the limbs of its body, and [...] universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fivefold, degree-like faculty list (mind/thought/insight/counsel/consideration) in an impersonal ‘produced and sent forth’ mechanics. The ‘rebels’ remain internal cosmic actors; the paragraph explains process, not ethics.

paragraphs.core_text: “And when they were sent, at [that ti]m[e] he was found with the Virgin of [Lig]ht and [he] stood up, asking and entreating for a p[o]wer. [ ... he] gave him peace and a ki[ss ...] he [gave] him goo[d] tidings [...] Man. The Man him[s]elf gave [his ...] his limbs and gathered his soul i[n ...] he built it in its place like this tower [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mythic-cosmic narrative remains system-internal (Virgin of Light; bestowal of power/peace; gathering of soul; building as ‘tower’). No institutional referents or audience-address pivot.

paragraphs.core_text: “[...] shaped it and beautified it skillfully [...] for[m ...] the voices that he sent [...] he might sink in and quench [... ...] so[u]l that was crushed by the enemy. They were gathered in. They came, set firm once more, in the image of their father.”
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic restoration mechanics (voices sent; soul ‘crushed by the enemy’; re-gathering; re-formation ‘in the image of their father’) continue the internal salvation architecture; the one pastoral-density blip likely reflects vocabulary noise rather than an institutional graft.
